# Auto routing

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:auto-routing` from lib/routing/policy.ts. Don't edit by hand. -->

Auto picks a model and reasoning effort for every message (`lib/routing/auto-router.ts`):

1. **Fast path**: obviously trivial messages ("hi", "thanks") skip classification: GPT-6 Luna, low.
2. **Classifier** (Settings → Auto Router, default GPT-OSS 20B on Groq): labels the latest message with a **task** (chat, factual, writing, coding, math, analysis, creative), a **difficulty** (trivial, standard, complex, expert) and whether it **needs deep thinking**. If it fails or takes over 3.5 s, keyword heuristics decide instead.
3. **Rules**: a request that contains or mentions code is a coding task, whatever the classifier said.
4. **Policy** (Settings → Auto Priority, default **Cost**): maps the labels to a model and effort, shown below. "Needs deep thinking" raises the effort one level on the same model. Premium models (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5) are only available when `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_EXPENSIVE_MODELS=true`; otherwise the policy falls back to the next model in line.

The chosen model and reason are shown in the message's model badge.

## Cost vs Performance

Default columns (premium models on, no deep thinking, no repository connected).

| Difficulty | Task | Cost (default) | Performance (first version) |
|---|---|---|---|
| trivial | chat | GPT-6 Luna, low | same |
| trivial | factual | GPT-6 Luna, low | same |
| trivial | writing | GPT-6 Luna, low | same |
| trivial | coding | GPT-6 Luna, low | same |
| trivial | math | GPT-6 Luna, low | same |
| trivial | analysis | GPT-6 Luna, low | same |
| trivial | creative | GPT-6 Luna, low | same |
| standard | chat | GPT-6 Luna, medium | same |
| standard | factual | GPT-6 Luna, medium | same |
| standard | writing | GPT-6 Luna, medium | GPT-6.1 Terra, medium |
| standard | coding | GPT-6 Luna, medium | GPT-6.1 Terra, medium |
| standard | math | GPT-6 Luna, medium | same |
| standard | analysis | GPT-6 Luna, medium | same |
| standard | creative | GPT-6 Luna, medium | GPT-6.1 Terra, medium |
| complex | chat | GPT-6 Luna, high | GPT-6.1 Terra, medium |
| complex | factual | GPT-6 Luna, high | GPT-6.1 Terra, medium |
| complex | writing | GPT-6.1 Terra, medium | Claude Sonnet 5.5, medium |
| complex | coding | GPT-6.1 Terra, medium | GPT-6.1 Sol, high |
| complex | math | GPT-6.1 Terra, medium | GPT-6.1 Sol, high |
| complex | analysis | GPT-6.1 Terra, medium | GPT-6.1 Sol, high |
| complex | creative | GPT-6.1 Terra, medium | Claude Sonnet 5.5, medium |
| expert | chat | GPT-6.1 Sol, high | GPT-6 Astra, extra high |
| expert | factual | GPT-6.1 Sol, high | GPT-6 Astra, extra high |
| expert | writing | GPT-6.1 Sol, high | GPT-6 Astra, extra high |
| expert | coding | GPT-6.1 Sol, high | GPT-6 Astra, extra high |
| expert | math | GPT-6.1 Sol, high | GPT-6 Astra, extra high |
| expert | analysis | GPT-6.1 Sol, high | GPT-6 Astra, extra high |
| expert | creative | GPT-6.1 Sol, high | GPT-6 Astra, extra high |

**Cost** (the default since 2026-11-01): Luna handles everything up to standard difficulty, and more reasoning effort on a cheaper model is tried before a pricier model. Terra only takes complex work, Sol only expert work; Astra and Claude are never picked.

**Performance** (the first version of the new router): stronger models earlier. Terra for standard coding, writing and creative work, Sol for complex technical work, Claude Sonnet 5.5 for complex writing, Astra for expert work, and coding with a connected GitHub repository never on Luna.
